name: flagellar type III export gate
description: Membrane-embedded export gate that translocates the axial subunits of the flagellum (rod, hook and filament) across the cytoplasmic membrane. Without it no axial structure can be built.

name: flagellar export ATPase complex
description: Cytoplasmic ATPase complex that delivers export substrates to the gate. FliJ is deliberately not required: it is a small, poorly conserved escort whose orthology assignment is unreliable, and requiring it would report absent machinery in genomes that build flagella.

name: flagellar MS ring
description: The membrane and supramembrane ring that nucleates basal body assembly and houses the export apparatus.

name: flagellar basal body rod
description: The drive shaft that transmits torque from the motor across the cell envelope to the hook, together with the rod-MS ring junction protein.

name: flagellar C ring and switch complex
description: The cytoplasmic ring that couples the stator to the rotor and switches rotational sense. FliY, which replaces FliN in some Firmicutes, is not accepted as evidence because its KEGG orthologue K02424 is assigned to an L-cystine transport binding protein and is therefore not specific to the flagellar switch.

name: flagellar hook
description: The curved universal joint that transmits torque from the rod to the filament. FlgD is excluded because it is a transient assembly scaffold rather than a part of the finished structure.

name: flagellar hook-filament junction
description: The hook-associated proteins that adapt the hook to the filament; without them flagellin polymerises without being retained.

name: flagellar filament
description: The helical propeller: polymerised flagellin together with the distal cap that permits its ordered polymerisation.

name: flagellar stator torque generator
description: The membrane-anchored ion-conducting stator units that generate torque against the C ring. The curated claim is deliberately silent about the coupling ion; see the description of SYS_SF_FLAGELLAR_STATOR_MOTAB.

name: flagellar L and P rings
description: The outer membrane and peptidoglycan bushings through which the rod passes in a diderm envelope. Monoderms build a flagellum without them, which is why they belong to a separate architecture rather than being an optional part of one.

name: type IV prepilin peptidase
description: Cleaves and N-methylates the type IV prepilin leader, without which no pilin can be polymerised.

name: type IVa major pilin
description: The subunit polymerised into the pilus fibre.

name: type IVa pilus assembly ATPase
description: The cytoplasmic motor ATPase that powers pilus extension.

name: type IVa pilus inner membrane platform
description: The polytopic inner membrane protein that transfers pilin subunits from the membrane into the growing fibre.

name: type IVa pilus alignment subcomplex
description: The envelope-spanning subcomplex that aligns the inner membrane platform with the outer membrane secretin.

name: type IVa pilus secretin
description: The outer membrane channel through which the pilus fibre emerges.

name: type IVa pilus retraction ATPase
description: The ATPase that depolymerises the fibre. It is accessory to assembling a pilus and is therefore not required by the architecture; a genome without it is expected to build a pilus it cannot retract.

name: Lpt inner-membrane extraction
description: The LptB2FGC complex extracts lipopolysaccharide from the inner membrane and passes it into the trans-envelope bridge.

name: Lpt periplasmic bridge
description: LptA extends the periplasm-spanning hydrophobic groove that conducts lipopolysaccharide between the inner- and outer-membrane complexes.

name: Lpt outer-membrane translocon
description: The LptDE complex receives lipopolysaccharide from the bridge and inserts it into the outer leaflet of the outer membrane.

name: UDP-ManNAc donor supply
description: Provides UDP-N-acetylmannosamine for the conserved wall-teichoic-acid linkage unit through a non-hydrolysing UDP-GlcNAc 2-epimerase.

name: wall-teichoic-acid linkage-unit construction
description: TagO initiates the undecaprenyl-linked unit, TagA adds N-acetylmannosamine and TagB primes it with glycerol phosphate; all three roles are jointly required.

name: CDP-glycerol donor supply
description: TagD produces the CDP-glycerol used for the conserved glycerol-phosphate linkage step in ribitol-phosphate WTA assembly.

name: CDP-ribitol donor supply
description: TarJ produces ribitol 5-phosphate and TarI activates it as CDP-ribitol for ribitol-phosphate backbone construction.

name: Staphylococcus-type ribitol-WTA priming and polymerization
description: The Staphylococcus design uses TarF to add the glycerol-phosphate adaptor and bifunctional TarL to prime and extend the ribitol-phosphate chain.

name: W23-type ribitol-WTA priming and polymerization
description: The Bacillus subtilis W23 design uses TarK to prime the ribitol-phosphate chain and TarL to extend it; the two roles are jointly required.

name: wall-teichoic-acid export
description: The TagG/TagH ABC transporter exports the completed wall teichoic acid precursor across the cytoplasmic membrane.

name: wall-teichoic-acid attachment to peptidoglycan
description: An LCP-family ligase transfers the exported wall teichoic acid from its lipid carrier to peptidoglycan.

name: diglucosyldiacylglycerol anchor synthesis
description: A processive glycosyltransferase forms the diglucosyldiacylglycerol membrane anchor that distinguishes this LTA boundary from residual diacylglycerol-anchored material.

name: diglucosyldiacylglycerol anchor translocation
description: LtaA flips the glycolipid anchor across the cytoplasmic membrane so that extracellular polymerization can proceed from it.

name: lipoteichoic-acid poly(glycerol-phosphate) polymerization
description: LtaS transfers glycerol phosphate from phosphatidylglycerol to construct the membrane-anchored poly(glycerol-phosphate) LTA chain.

name: Type VI membrane complex
description: The envelope-spanning complex that anchors the baseplate and forms the channel through which the tube and spike are propelled.

name: Type VI outer-membrane lipoprotein
description: The TssJ lipoprotein that completes the membrane complex in many proteobacteria. It is accessory to the curated architecture: Agrobacterium and Acinetobacter reference genomes, whose apparatus is experimentally active, carry no TssJ marker in either namespace, so requiring it would report an absent machine in genomes that build one.

name: Type VI baseplate
description: The assembly platform that docks on the membrane complex and from which the tube and sheath polymerise.

name: Type VI spike
description: The VgrG trimer that caps the tube and is expelled with it. PAAR tip proteins are not required: no admitted marker is specific to them.

name: Type VI inner tube
description: The stack of Hcp hexamers that is propelled out of the cell.

name: Type VI contractile sheath
description: The TssB/TssC sheath whose contraction propels the tube.

name: Type VI assembly coordination
description: TssA primes and coordinates the polymerisation of the tube and the sheath from the baseplate.

name: Type VI sheath recycling
description: The ClpV ATPase that disassembles the contracted sheath. It is required rather than accessory because ClpV-mediated remodelling of the sheath is experimentally crucial for type VI secretion.

name: Injectisome export apparatus
description: The inner-membrane export gate through which substrates enter the secretion channel.

name: Injectisome export ATPase
description: The cytoplasmic ATPase that prepares substrates for export. The SctL stator that tethers it is deliberately not required: its orthology assignment does not reach the Inv-Mxi-Spa and Esc families in either namespace, and requiring it would report an absent machine in genomes that build an injectisome.

name: Injectisome inner-membrane rings
description: The two concentric rings that house the export apparatus in the inner membrane.

name: Injectisome outer-membrane secretin
description: The outer-membrane ring through which the filament emerges. The flagellum has no homologue of it.

name: Injectisome sorting platform
description: The cytoplasmic platform protein that orders substrates for secretion. SctK is not required because its orthology assignment is unreliable.

name: Injectisome inner rod
description: The short rod that connects the export apparatus to the extracellular filament inside the basal body.

name: Injectisome extracellular filament
description: The hollow filament that carries substrates away from the cell surface: a needle in animal-associated systems or an Hrp pilus in plant-associated ones.

name: archaellum filament
description: The archaellin subunit polymerised into the rotating filament. Archaellin glycosylation is not required: it modifies the filament without being part of the assembly machinery.

name: archaellin class III signal peptidase
description: Removes the class III signal peptide from prearchaellins; unprocessed archaellins are not assembled (PMID 14622420). The enzyme is a shared component, not part of the finished structure: PibD also processes archaeal type IV pilins and other class III substrates (PMID 12813086), so the function contributes no machine specificity to the call.

name: archaellum FlaF/FlaG stator complex
description: The membrane-anchored FlaF/FlaG complex that holds the motor against the cell envelope during rotation (PMID 34912317).

name: archaellum FlaI/FlaH motor complex
description: The cytoplasmic FlaI hexameric ATPase that powers assembly and rotation, together with the KaiC-like FlaH that regulates it. FlaI is homologous to the assembly ATPases of archaeal type IV pili.

name: archaellum FlaJ membrane platform
description: The polytopic membrane protein on which the motor assembles. FlaJ is homologous to the platform proteins of archaeal type IV pili.

name: euryarchaeal FlaC/D/E switch complex
description: The euryarchaeal cytoplasmic ring that receives chemotaxis input through CheF and acts as the switch complex (PMID 32416640). It is required for archaellation in Methanococcus maripaludis (PMID 17887963) but absent or unassigned in Methanomicrobiales, most Methanosarcinales and every crenarchaeal and thaumarchaeal archaellum, so it is accessory to the core machinery. Rotational switching is outside the claim.

name: crenarchaeal FlaX ring
description: The crenarchaeal cytoplasmic ring that scaffolds the motor and binds FlaI. It is required in Sulfolobus acidocaldarius (PMID 22081969) but has no KEGG orthology, so it is accessory: no architecture may depend on a function the reference frame cannot measure.

name: Type II secretion outer-membrane secretin
description: The GspD channel through which folded substrates cross the outer membrane. The GspS pilotin that targets it in some lineages is not required: it is absent from systems that assemble a secretin without it.

name: Type II secretion inner-membrane platform
description: The GspC, GspF, GspL and GspM proteins that span the inner membrane, connect the secretin to the ATPase and are jointly required. GspN is excluded as a non-universal accessory protein.

name: Type II secretion ATPase
description: The cytoplasmic GspE ATPase that powers pseudopilus extension.

name: Type II secretion pseudopilus
description: The major pseudopilin GspG together with the minor pseudopilins GspH, GspI, GspJ and GspK, whose tip complex primes elongation of the piston that pushes substrate through the secretin.

name: Type II secretion pseudopilin maturation
description: Cleavage and N-methylation of the class III pseudopilin leader peptides, without which no pseudopilus can be polymerised. The enzyme is a shared component: the same protein also processes type IVa pilins, so this function contributes no specificity to either machine and the apparatus is identified by its other four functions.
